title: Who must appoint a chemical substance manager in Japan, and what training do they need?
description: Japan 2024 chemical reforms: chemical substance manager and protective equipment manager duties, the 12 hour course, 6 hour PPE training and records.
shortAnswer: Since April 1, 2024, every Japanese workplace that manufactures, handles or supplies chemicals subject to risk assessment must appoint a chemical substance manager (kagaku busshitsu kanrisha) within 14 days under article 12-5 of the Ordinance on Industrial Safety and Health. At manufacturing sites the manager must complete a 12 hour ministerial course. Where protective equipment is used as a control, a protective equipment manager must also be appointed under article 12-6.
keyTakeaways: Article 12-5 of the Ordinance requires a chemical substance manager at each workplace that manufactures or handles risk assessment target substances, and at workplaces that only supply them, appointed within 14 days of the trigger.

At manufacturing sites the manager must have completed the course in MHLW Notice No. 276 of 2022 (9 lecture hours and 3 practical hours) or be recognized as equivalent; the practical part cannot be done online.

Article 12-6 requires a protective equipment manager (hogogu chakuyō kanri sekininsha) wherever workers use protective equipment as a risk assessment control; MHLW's curriculum for those without listed qualifications totals 6 hours.
Both appointees must be given the authority to do the job and their names must be made known to workers, for example by posting in a visible place.
The chemical substance manager's duties include managing the education workers need on labels, safety data sheets, risk assessment and exposure controls.
regulator: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW), enforced by Labor Standards Inspection Offices under each Prefectural Labor Bureau
appliesTo: Workplaces in any industry that manufacture or handle risk assessment target substances, including laboratories, hospitals, cleaning, printing, construction and auto repair
Workplaces that sell or supply those substances, for the labeling and safety data sheet duties
Appointed chemical substance managers and protective equipment managers
EHS, industrial hygiene and training teams responsible for chemical safety education

sections.heading: What did Japan's chemical management reforms change on April 1, 2024?

blocks.text: The reforms moved Japan from substance by substance rules toward self managed chemical risk control, and they created two new statutory appointments. The Ordinance Partially Amending the Ordinance on Industrial Safety and Health (MHLW Ordinance No. 91 of 2022), promulgated on May 31, 2022, phased in the changes, with the chemical substance manager and protective equipment manager provisions taking effect on April 1, 2024 ([MHLW implementation circular Kihatsu 0531 No. 9](https://www.mhlw.go.jp/content/11300000/000987120.pdf)).

The implementation circular explains the policy reason: roughly 80 percent of chemical accidents causing four or more days of lost work involved substances outside the specific regulations such as the Ordinance on Prevention of Organic Solvent Poisoning. The answer was to require risk assessment and exposure minimization for a much wider list of substances, and to appoint a named person at each site to manage it. This page describes the rules as at November 2026.

The same reform made hiring education on chemical hazards compulsory in every industry from April 1, 2024, covered in [Japan's new hire safety and health education](/regulations/japan-new-hire-safety-and-health-education). The wider education framework is on the [Industrial Safety and Health Act page](/regulations/japan-industrial-safety-and-health-act-training).

sections.heading: Which workplaces must appoint a chemical substance manager?

blocks.text: Every workplace (事業場) that manufactures or handles a risk assessment target substance must appoint one, regardless of size or industry. Article 12-5(1) of the Ordinance on Industrial Safety and Health (労働安全衛生規則) defines these substances as those listed in article 18 of the Enforcement Order and the notification substances under article 57-2 of the Act ([Ordinance, e-Gov](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/347M50002000032)). Article 12-5(2) adds workplaces that only transfer or supply such substances, for labeling and safety data sheet matters.

items: **Handling includes enclosed processes:** the circular states that a sealed or automated process still counts as handling if a handling operation exists, even where workers are not exposed.

**Exclusions:** workplaces that only handle products for general consumer use, that only store sealed containers without opening them, or that handle substances only temporarily in emergency response are not caught.
**Split sites:** if labels are prepared at a different site from the factory, each site needs its own manager for its share of the duties.
**Timing:** article 12-5(3)(i) requires appointment within 14 days of the event that triggers the duty.

sections.heading: What does a chemical substance manager do?

blocks.text: The manager runs the technical side of chemical management at the site. Article 12-5(1) lists seven duties: labels, safety data sheets and notifications; carrying out risk assessment; the exposure reduction measures in article 577-2; response to chemical accidents; creating, keeping and communicating risk assessment records; keeping the exposure and measures records under article 577-2(11); and "the education workers need" to support the first four duties.

The education duty is a management duty, not a teaching duty. The circular states that the manager must plan and manage the necessary education but need not deliver it personally, and that workers can be sent to an external provider. It also confirms that education already given through hiring education before 2024 does not have to be repeated. Article 12-5(4) requires the employer to give the manager the authority needed, and article 12-5(5) requires the manager's name to be made known to workers, which the circular says can be by posting, an armband, a distinctive helmet or the intranet.

Related records carry their own retention rules. Article 34-2-8 requires the risk assessment record to be kept until the next assessment, or for three years if the next one comes within three years. Article 577-2(11) requires an annual record of measures and exposure, kept for three years, or 30 years for carcinogenic substances designated by the Minister.

sections.heading: What training must a chemical substance manager complete?

blocks.text: At a site that manufactures risk assessment target substances, the manager must have completed the course set by the Minister or be recognized as having equivalent or greater ability (article 12-5(3)(ii)(a)). The course is defined in MHLW Notice No. 276 of 2022, issued September 7, 2022 and applying from April 1, 2024 ([MHLW Notice No. 276 of 2022](https://www.mhlw.go.jp/content/11300000/000987097.pdf)).

blocks.text: The total is 12 hours. Workers who completed all three operations chief skill training courses for organic solvents, lead, and specified chemicals and tetraalkyl lead are exempt from the first subject; holders of a first class health officer license are exempt from the risk assessment subject; and holders of a health engineering health officer license are exempt from that subject and the measures subject.

MHLW's application circular adds that lectures may be delivered online but the practical session may not, that it is desirable to assess learner understanding, and that the employer should keep a record of the date, provider, subjects, content and hours so a third party can confirm the appointee qualifies ([MHLW circular Kihatsu 0907 No. 1, revised July 14, 2023](https://www.mhlw.go.jp/content/11300000/001117847.pdf)).

blocks.title: Non manufacturing sites
blocks.text: At sites that handle but do not manufacture these substances, article 12-5(3)(ii)(b) allows anyone with the necessary ability. The circular recommends a comparable course and gives a guide curriculum that totals 6 hours of lectures, or lectures combined with practical work, covering the same five lecture subjects.

The circular also recognizes as equivalent people who took the course before it formally applied, registered occupational health consultants in the industrial hygiene engineering category, and people who meet the chemical management expert criteria in MHLW Notice No. 274 of 2022.

sections.heading: When is a protective equipment manager required, and what training applies?

blocks.text: An employer that has appointed a chemical substance manager must also appoint a protective equipment manager whenever it has workers use protective equipment as a measure based on risk assessment (article 12-6(1)). The manager oversees selection, correct use and maintenance of the equipment, must be appointed within 14 days from among people with knowledge and experience of protective equipment, and must be given authority and be made known to workers.

The implementation circular lists who counts as having that knowledge and experience, including chemical management experts, occupational health consultants, first class or health engineering health officers, certain operations chiefs and safety and health promoters, and recommends further training even for them. Anyone outside those groups must complete the protective equipment manager education before appointment. MHLW set its curriculum in a circular of December 26, 2022 ([MHLW circular Kian Kahatsu 1226 No. 1](https://www.mhlw.go.jp/content/11300000/001031069.pdf)).

blocks.text: The classroom part may be delivered online and may be split from the practical part, provided the practical session is only for people who finished the classroom subjects and identity can be confirmed. Respiratory protection material should cover Japanese Industrial Standard T 8150. An employer that runs the education itself should keep a record of participants and subjects; an external provider should issue a completion document and keep a register.

sections.heading: What happens if inspectors find chemical management inadequate?

blocks.text: The Labor Standards Inspection Office chief can order improvement. Under article 34-2-10, a workplace that has had, or risks, a chemical accident and appears to be managing chemicals poorly can be instructed to improve; it must then obtain a review and advice from a chemical management expert, make an improvement plan within one month of the written advice, report the plan to the inspection office, and keep records of the measures for three years. The circular gives examples of triggers, such as repeated lost time chemical injuries within about a year.
Training records are among the first documents such a review examines, which is a practical reason to keep the manager's course record and the workforce education plan in the same place.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links each risk assessment target substance, task and control to the roles affected and to the education the chemical substance manager must plan. When a substance is added to the target list or a control changes from engineering to protective equipment, the framework shows which appointments, curricula and records are now required.

faqs.q: Can one person be the chemical substance manager for several workplaces?
faqs.a: Article 12-5 requires appointment for each workplace. The implementation circular allows the duties to be shared among several managers at a large site, with coordination to avoid gaps, and allows parts of the practical work to be contracted to outside experts under the manager's control. Its own example of a factory and a separate labeling office requires a manager at each of the two workplaces.

faqs.q: Can an operations chief also be the protective equipment manager?
faqs.a: Yes. The implementation circular states that an operations chief may also serve as protective equipment manager where this does not impair either role, and that a large workplace may appoint more than one protective equipment manager so the duties can be carried out properly.

faqs.q: Is the chemical substance manager course a skill training course?
faqs.a: No. It is not a skill training course under article 61 and no registered training body is required. The employer may run the course itself or send the manager to another provider's course, as long as the subjects, hours and instructor capability in MHLW Notice No. 276 of 2022 are met.

faqs.q: Does an office that only stores sealed chemicals need a chemical substance manager?
faqs.a: According to the implementation circular, simply storing sealed products without opening containers does not count as manufacturing or handling, so it does not trigger article 12-5(1). If the site supplies those products to others, however, article 12-5(2) may still require a manager for labeling and safety data sheet duties.

factCheck.claim: Ordinance article 12-5(1) requires a chemical substance manager at each workplace manufacturing or handling risk assessment target substances (Order art. 18 substances and Act art. 57-2 notification substances), with seven duties including (vii) education of workers; 12-5(2) covers supply only workplaces; 12-5(3) appointment within 14 days, manufacturing sites from course completers or equivalent; 12-5(4) authority; 12-5(5) publicize name.

Ordinance article 12-6 requires a protective equipment manager where protective equipment is used as a risk assessment based measure, appointed within 14 days from people with knowledge and experience, managing selection, use and maintenance, with authority and publicized name. Article 34-2-8 risk assessment records kept until next assessment or 3 years; article 577-2(11) annual records kept 3 years or 30 years for carcinogens; article 34-2-10 improvement instruction, expert advice, plan within one month, records 3 years.

MHLW Ordinance No. 91 of 2022 was promulgated May 31, 2022 with parts effective April 1, 2023 and April 1, 2024; detailed matters for April 1, 2024 include the chemical substance manager and protective equipment manager; about 80 percent of lost time chemical accidents involved substances outside the special regulations; the manager need not personally deliver education; handling includes enclosed processes; exclusions for sealed storage and emergency only handling; posting can be by armband, helmet or intranet; list of persons with protective equipment knowledge and experience; operations chiefs may double as protective equipment managers.

MHLW Notice No. 276 of 2022 (September 7, 2022, applying April 1, 2024) sets lectures of 2.5, 3, 2, 0.5 and 1 hours and a 3 hour practical, with subject exemptions for holders of all three chemical operations chief courses, first class health officers and health engineering health officers.

Circular Kihatsu 0907 No. 1 states lectures may be online but practicals may not; assessment of understanding is desirable; course records should be kept; equivalents include pre application course completers, industrial hygiene engineering consultants and chemical management experts; non manufacturing sites should preferably use a guide course totaling 6 hours.

Protective equipment manager education (Kian Kahatsu 1226 No. 1, December 26, 2022): classroom 0.5, 3, 1 and 0.5 hours plus 1 hour practical, total 6 hours; classroom may be online; JIS T 8150 for respirators; records and completion documents.
